title: Congruent dissections of a triangle: prime counts, the counts up to 200, and a family of isosceles targets
description: A positive integer N is a tile count if some triangle can be cut into N pairwise congruent triangles; Erdős asked for the set of tile counts (Problem 634). The problem is not solved here. With every cited step checked in Lean 4 against the standard axioms only: (1) a prime p is a tile count if and only if p = 3 or p ≢ 3 (mod 4); (2) for 1 ≤ N ≤ 200 the tile counts are exactly 105 explicit values (the last value settled, 135, is excluded by a kernel-checked search certificate); (3) for a tile with angles (α, β, 2π/3), α/π irrational, a signed-direction functional gives two integrality conditions, and no prime number of such tiles tiles an isosceles, non-equilateral triangle; (4) for the base-β targets T_M(e,f) tiled by (ef, f²−e², f²), a tiling exists for every M ≥ f, none for M = 1, none when 2Me < f. Version 3.0 (paper `erdos634_v3`) adds, in Lean for all parameters: tilings of W_M(e,f) and T_M(e,f) below the scale f for 2 ≤ e ≤ f−2 when Me ≥ f and (M−1)(f−e) ≥ f (sharp for e < f/2), a collar family for the base-α targets (the up-set in the scale is Paliy's), 27 further tile counts by macro pieces, the existence half of a conjectured classification of the tile counts (the exclusion half is open), a census update (199,140 excluded / 129,108 tile counts / 63,826 undecided among the non-squarefree N ≤ 10^6), exact computer evidence on one open family, and a list of corrections. The prime case is unchanged. A proof of (1) was first made public by D. Paliy on 29 September 2026; the proof here was obtained independently. The repository contains the paper, the Lean library, the certificate manifest with a regeneration script, and the Rust search and replay programs. The work was carried out with the assistance of Claude (Anthropic) throughout, under the author's direction.
